title: HE WILL ATTACK THEM AT THEIR HEELS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Gad will be attacked by a band of raiders, but he will attack them at their heels.'" — Gen 49:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short line, and it holds a whole way of living. Gad will be attacked — and Gad will get back up and pursue.

The tribe of Gad settled on the eastern side of the Jordan, exposed territory, and they became known as fierce and faithful fighters. Attack was simply part of their situation. What defined them was not that they avoided it but that they did not stay down.

That is a realistic picture of the Christian life. Scripture never promises believers a life free from opposition. Jesus said plainly, "In this world you will have trouble" — and then added, "But take heart! I have overcome the world" (Jn 16:33).

The question is not whether you will be knocked down, but what happens next.

Proverbs says the righteous fall seven times and rise again (Prov 24:16). Note that it does not say the righteous never fall. Their distinguishing mark is that they keep getting up.

If you have been knocked down recently — by failure, by opposition, by discouragement — the important thing is not that it happened. It is that you get up. And you do not do it in your own strength; God is the one who strengthens and steadies His people (1 Pet 5:10).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has knocked you down recently?
2. Do you expect the Christian life to be free of opposition?
3. What would getting back up look like this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I am tired of being knocked down. Strengthen me to rise again, not in my own strength but in Yours, and keep me facing forward. Amen.
